findings.summary: Thimble achieves higher long-tail Recall@20 (0.091) than Cobble-GNN with uniform sampling (0.072) and Cobble-GNN with debiased sampling (0.085) on Garnet-Retail.
findings.scope: Garnet-Retail test split, long-tail Recall@20, mean of 3 runs

findings.summary: Adding debiased sampling to Cobble-GNN improves long-tail Recall@20 from 0.072 to 0.085, a relative gain of about 18%, which is consistent with the roughly 20% relative gains attributed to popularity-debiased negative sampling in prior work.

passages.source_title: Sampling Against the Head: Popularity-Debiased Negatives for Recommendation
passages.text: On both datasets we studied, popularity-debiased negative sampling reduced training time per epoch by 21% relative to uniform negative sampling, because negatives are drawn from a precomputed alias table. Overall Recall@20 changed by less than 1% on both datasets.

decision.revised_text: Adding popularity-debiased negative sampling to Cobble-GNN raises long-tail Recall@20 from 0.072 to 0.085 on the Garnet-Retail test split, a relative gain of about 18% (no statistical test was reported).
decision.rationale: Numbers and 18% relative gain verified (0.072→0.085, 18.06%). However, no statistical test was reported for exp1/cmp2, so "improves" (implying significance) is unsupported. Also, P1 attributes ~21% gains to training time, not long-tail Recall@20; the "consistent with ~20% relative gains" attribution is unsupported by the supplied passage.
